pr.title: coverage: Detect unused local file IDs to avoid an LLVM assertion
pr.description:
Each function's coverage metadata contains a *local file table* that maps local file IDs (used by the function's mapping regions) to global file IDs (shared by all functions in the same CGU).

LLVM requires all local file IDs to have at least one mapping region, and has an assertion that will fail if it detects a local file ID with no regions. To make sure that assertion doesn't fire, we need to detect and skip functions whose metadata would trigger it.

(This can't actually happen yet, because currently all of a function's spans must belong to the same file and expansion. But this will be an important edge case when adding expansion region support.)
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Coverage metadata must not emit a function whose local file table contains a local file ID with no mapping region, because LLVM asserts on unused local file IDs. The fix detects such functions (via `check_local_file_table` over all coverage spans) and skips their covfun record, and moves empty-span enlargement from LLVM codegen into the InstrumentCoverage MIR span pipeline so spans are non-empty before merge/dedup. Downstream MIR (e.g. CleanupPostBorrowck dumps) sees the enlarged spans.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, empty coverage spans were handled only during LLVM codegen: `make_coords` called `ensure_non_empty_span` to enlarge an empty span over an adjacent `{`/`}`, otherwise returning `None` and dropping it. `generate_covfun_record` emitted the function's coverage metadata unconditionally, and there was no check that every local file ID in the function's `virtual_file_mapping.local_file_table` was referenced by at least one mapping region. `has_no_regions` checked each region table separately.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to emit a function's coverage metadata even when some local file ID in its local file table had no associated mapping region (for example, because empty spans were dropped late at codegen, or because an unused file entry existed), which violates LLVM's invariant and can trigger an assertion. The fix does not perform a different source rewrite: it adds `check_local_file_table`, which builds a bool `IndexVec` over `local_file_table.len()`, marks `cov_span.file_id` for all spans, and returns false if any entry is unseen; `generate_covfun_record` then returns early, skipping that function. It also relocates empty-span enlargement from `make_coords` in codegen to `extract_refined_covspans` in the InstrumentCoverage MIR pass, before `dedup_by`/`merge_if_eligible`, so non-empty spans can merge.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with coverage instrumentation (`-Cinstrument-coverage`), especially functions whose coverage spans include empty spans at source positions adjacent to `{` or `}`, and functions that may eventually have multiple local file IDs due to expansion regions. The regression test adds `-Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file` to inject a dummy unused local file table entry.
analysis.trigger: A function's coverage `local_file_table` contains at least one local file ID that no `CoverageSpan`/region references (e.g. an injected dummy file entry, or a file whose spans were all dropped), so LLVM's assertion about local file IDs with no mapping regions would fire if the covfun record were emitted.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled, e.g. via `-Cinstrument-coverage`.
The function has coverage metadata with a `CovfunRecord`/`virtual_file_mapping` local file table.
At least one local file ID in that per-function table is unreferenced by any region's `cov_span.file_id`.
The unused-local-file condition can be forced with `-Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file` (testing-only flag).
Empty coverage spans may arise from source positions where the span start equals the span end.
pitfalls: Skipping the entire covfun record is intentional when `check_local_file_table` fails; do not merely delete the unused local file table entry, because the PR explicitly chooses to skip the function.
`check_local_file_table` indexes a bool vector sized to `covfun.virtual_file_mapping.local_file_table.len()` using `cov_span.file_id`; local file IDs must remain valid per-function indices.

Moving `ensure_non_empty_span` into the InstrumentCoverage MIR pipeline happens before `dedup_by`/`merge_if_eligible`, so previously separate mappings can merge; e.g. the async_closure `.cov-map` drops from two mappings to one.
Codegen now uses `if span.is_empty() { debug_assert!(false, ...); return None; }` instead of enlarging; the assertion only fires in debug builds, so release behavior silently discards the span.
`has_no_regions` was refactored to `self.all_cov_spans().next().is_none()`, so all region tables must be included in `all_cov_spans` for the empty check to remain correct.
The test-only inject flag must be paired with an auxiliary instrumented crate; otherwise `llvm-cov` complains if the test binary has no coverage metadata at all.
Downstream pass dumps such as CleanupPostBorrowck are affected by InstrumentCoverage's earlier span enlargement even though CleanupPostBorrowck's logic did not change.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*` expectations to pin exact span coordinates after InstrumentCoverage and in downstream CleanupPostBorrowck dumps: previously empty spans such as `21:2: 21:2` and `15:2: 15:2` must become non-empty `21:1: 21:2` and `15:1: 15:2`, demonstrating enlargement over the adjacent brace. Use `tests/coverage/unused-local-file.rs` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file` plus `//@ aux-build: discard_all_helper.rs` and `extern crate discard_all_helper;` so the test binary still has real coverage metadata while the injected unused local file exercises the skip path. Check `.cov-map` outputs for merged mappings (e.g. async_closure goes from two file-0 mappings to one). This analysis is static; no compiler was built or tests executed.
